title: Angles in a Circle and Cyclic Quadrilaterals
summary: The angle an arc (or chord) makes at the centre is the central angle; the angle it makes at a point on the remaining part of the circle is an inscribed angle. Points that lie on one circle are concyclic.

(1) The angle subtended by an arc at the centre is double the angle it subtends at any point on the remaining part of the circle: ∠AOB = 2∠ACB. So if an arc subtends x° at the centre and y° on the circle, x = 2y.
(2) The angle in a semicircle is a right angle (the diameter subtends 180° at the centre, so 90° on the circle).
(3) Angles in the same segment of a circle are equal.
(4) The opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add up to 180°.
(5) Converse: if a pair of opposite angles of a quadrilateral is supplementary, the quadrilateral is cyclic.
(6) An exterior angle of a cyclic quadrilateral equals the interior opposite angle.
## Proof: angles in the same segment are equal
Let ∠ACB and ∠ADB be in the same segment of a circle with centre O. Join OA and OB. By theorem (1), ∠AOB = 2∠ACB and ∠AOB = 2∠ADB. Therefore 2∠ACB = 2∠ADB, so ∠ACB = ∠ADB.
## Proof: opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary

Let ABCD be cyclic with centre O. Join OB and OD. Arc BAD subtends ∠BOD = 2∠BCD at the centre, and arc BCD subtends the reflex angle BOD = 2∠BAD. The two angles at O together make 360°, so 2∠BCD + 2∠BAD = 360°, i.e. ∠A + ∠C = 180°. Similarly ∠B + ∠D = 180°.

A chord equal to the radius forms an equilateral triangle with the centre, so it subtends 60° at the centre, 30° at a point on the major arc and 150° at a point on the minor arc. Radii are equal, so a triangle with two radii as sides is isosceles: if ∠BAC = 35°, ∠BOC = 70° and ∠OBC = (180° − 70°)/2 = 55°. Of the parallelograms only the rectangle (and square) is cyclic, because its opposite angles are 90° + 90°. When a triangle stands on a diameter, Pythagoras gives the diameter: AC = 3, BC = 4 ⇒ AB = 5, radius 2.5.
mcq: Angles in the same segment of a circle are —

mcq.work: By the theorem, every angle subtended by the same arc in the same segment equals half the central angle, so they are all equal.

mcq.work: The diameter subtends 180° at the centre, so it subtends 180°/2 = 90° at any point on the circle.

mcq.work: A quadrilateral is cyclic when opposite angles are supplementary. In a rectangle each angle is 90°, so 90° + 90° = 180° ✓. A general parallelogram or rhombus does not satisfy this.

mcq: AOB is a diameter of a circle with centre O. If AC = 3 cm and BC = 4 cm (C on the circle), the radius is —

mcq.work:
∠ACB = 90° (angle in a semicircle).
AB² = 3² + 4² = 25 ⇒ AB = 5 cm (diameter). Radius = 2.5 cm.

objective: Fill in the blanks: (i) In cyclic quadrilateral ABCD, ∠DAB = 110°, so ∠BCD = ____. (ii) AB is a chord of a circle with centre O, ∠OAB = 40° and C is on the major arc; ∠ACB = ____.

(i) Opposite angles are supplementary: 180° − 110° = 70°.
(ii) OA = OB, so ∠OBA = 40° and ∠AOB = 180° − 80° = 100°; ∠ACB = ½ × 100° = 50°.
Write True or False: (i) A chord equal to the radius subtends 30° at a point on the minor arc. (ii) ∠PAQ = 35° is inscribed in a circle with centre O standing on chord PQ; then ∠OPQ = 50°.

(i) False: the central angle is 60°; on the major arc the angle is 30°, on the minor arc it is 180° − 30° = 150°.
(ii) False: ∠POQ = 2 × 35° = 70°; OP = OQ, so ∠OPQ = (180° − 70°)/2 = 55°.
Fill in the blanks: (i) In cyclic quadrilateral PQRS, side PS is produced to A and ∠PQR = 80°; ∠ASR = ____. (ii) If ∠R = 78°, then ∠P = ____.

(i) An exterior angle of a cyclic quadrilateral equals the interior opposite angle: ∠ASR = ∠PQR = 80°. (Also ∠PSR = 100°, so ∠ASR = 180° − 100° = 80°.)
(ii) ∠P + ∠R = 180° ⇒ ∠P = 102°.
Fill in the blanks: (i) In cyclic quadrilateral ABCD, ∠DBC = 55° and ∠BAC = 45°; then ∠BCD = ____. (ii) The angle subtended at the centre by a semicircle is a ____ angle.

Join the chord's ends A and B to the centre O. OA = OB = AB, so △OAB is equilateral and ∠AOB = 60°.

sa: Prove that angles in the same segment of a circle are equal.

Given: a circle with centre O; ∠ACB and ∠ADB are in the same segment, standing on arc AB.
To prove: ∠ACB = ∠ADB.
Construction: join OA and OB.
Proof: the angle subtended by an arc at the centre is double the angle subtended at any point on the remaining circle.
So ∠AOB = 2∠ACB and ∠AOB = 2∠ADB.
Hence 2∠ACB = 2∠ADB, i.e. ∠ACB = ∠ADB. Proved.
Prove that the opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary.

Given: ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral, centre O.
To prove: ∠A + ∠C = 180° and ∠B + ∠D = 180°.
Construction: join OB and OD.
Proof: arc BCD subtends ∠BOD (marked x) at the centre and ∠BAD on the circle, so ∠BAD = ½x.
Arc BAD subtends the reflex angle (360° − x) at the centre and ∠BCD on the circle, so ∠BCD = ½(360° − x).
Adding: ∠A + ∠C = ½x + 180° − ½x = 180°.
Since the angles of a quadrilateral add to 360°, ∠B + ∠D = 360° − 180° = 180°. Proved.
ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral in which AB is a diameter and ∠ADC = 130°. Find ∠BAC.

∠ABC = 180° − ∠ADC = 50° (opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral).
∠ACB = 90° (angle in a semicircle).
In △ABC: ∠BAC = 180° − 90° − 50° = 40°.
la: Prove that the angle subtended by an arc at the centre of a circle is double the angle subtended by it at any point on the remaining part of the circle.

Given: arc AB of a circle with centre O; C is a point on the remaining part.
To prove: ∠AOB = 2∠ACB.
Construction: join CO and produce it to a point D.
Proof: in △OAC, OA = OC (radii), so ∠OAC = ∠OCA.
The exterior angle ∠AOD = ∠OAC + ∠OCA = 2∠OCA …(1)
Similarly in △OBC, ∠BOD = 2∠OCB …(2)
Adding (1) and (2): ∠AOD + ∠BOD = 2(∠OCA + ∠OCB), i.e. ∠AOB = 2∠ACB. Proved.
(For a major arc, the same steps give reflex ∠AOB = 2∠ACB.)
Two circles intersect at A and B. AC and AD are diameters of the two circles. Prove that C, B and D are collinear.

Join AB, BC and BD.
AC is a diameter of the first circle, so ∠ABC = 90° (angle in a semicircle).
AD is a diameter of the second circle, so ∠ABD = 90°.
∠ABC + ∠ABD = 90° + 90° = 180°, so CBD is a straight line.
Hence C, B and D are collinear.
